record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.original_question: How can rigorous mathematical sketches of self-referential biological organization, such as Rosen’s metabolism-repair systems interpreted through fixed points, domain theory, or coalgebras, be bridged to plausible biological mechanisms, and when should concurrent-process formalisms replace rigid sequential function application for modeling autopoiesis?

evidence.quote:
It is possible to find a λ-calculus term providing a uniform
solution to these equations, making use of the fixpoint (or ‘paradoxical’) combinator Y [122]. This in
turn can be interpreted mathematically in terms of domain theory. Related ways of interpreting ( M, R)
systems using coalgebras in the guise of non-well-founded sets are described in [123]. Thus we see some
lineaments of a rigorous theory underpinning Rosen’s ideas using the mathematics of self-reference. A
remaining challenge is to bridge the (large) gap between these mathematical sketches and plausible
biological mechanisms.

As those authors note, it may be more natural to use an approach based on
concurrent processes, rather than the more rigid and sequential notion of function application.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Rosen's metabolism-repair systems (M,R-systems) model a living organism as a closed network of mappings in which metabolism, repair, and replication are mutually defining. Concretely, given sets A (inputs/metabolites) and B (outputs), one considers a metabolism map f : A → B, a repair map Φ : B → H(A,B) (where H(A,B) denotes the set of admissible maps A → B), and a replication map β : H(A,B) → H(B, H(A,B)), subject to the closure condition that the entire diagram be reproduced from within: there exist b ∈ B such that Φ(b) = f and β(f)(b) = Φ. Such systems can be assigned uniform solutions via the fixed-point combinator Y of the untyped λ-calculus, interpreted in Scott-style domain theory, and alternatively modelled coalgebraically using non-well-founded (anti-foundation) set theory.

Problem. (a) Construct an explicit mathematical bridge between the above formal sketches of self-referential organization (λ-calculus / domain-theoretic fixed points, and coalgebraic / non-well-founded set models of (M,R)-systems) and concrete classes of biological mechanisms (e.g. enzymatic reaction networks, autocatalytic chemical reaction systems, gene-regulatory feedback loops), in the form of a faithful interpretation functor or simulation theorem that preserves the closure-to-efficient-causation property of (M,R)-systems.

(b) Identify precise mathematical criteria under which a sequential, function-application based formalism (λ-calculus, ordinary recursion) is inadequate for modelling autopoietic organization, and must be replaced by a concurrent-process formalism (such as the π-calculus, CCS, Petri nets, or bigraphs); in particular, formulate and prove a separation theorem exhibiting an autopoietic phenomenon expressible in a concurrent-process model but not realisable as a fixed point of any sequential λ-term up to observational equivalence.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicitly open challenge: while λ-calculus/domain-theoretic and coalgebraic (non-well-founded set) formalizations of Rosen's (M,R)-systems exist (e.g. work by Mossio, Letelier and collaborators, and Baianu), no general bridge to concrete biological mechanisms has been established, and the suitability of concurrent-process calculi (π-calculus, etc.) for autopoiesis remains a programmatic suggestion rather than a theorem. No source verifying a resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Organizational invariance and metabolic closure (Letelier et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses (M,R)-systems, fixed-point characterizations and open problems regarding biological realization.
status_evidence.claim: The mathematical theory of (M,R)-systems via fixed points is still being related to actual biological mechanisms; bridging remains open.

status_evidence.title: Rosen's (M,R) system in process algebra (Cárdenas et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes process-algebraic / concurrent reformulations of (M,R)-systems, noting limitations of sequential function application.
status_evidence.claim: Concurrent-process reformulations are proposed but a general theorem replacing sequential λ-calculus with concurrent calculi for autopoiesis has not been established.
